text: Scheduled reports are handed to the user as an S3 pre-signed URL valid for 24 hours, never as an email attachment: our mail gateway rejects anything over 25 MB and a monthly report for a large account is 200-400 MB.
Report rendering runs on a dedicated worker pool, not on the API instances: a single large render pins a core for 40+ seconds and was starving request handlers during business hours.

We render with WeasyPrint and rejected Chrome-headless: headless needs ~400 MB of RAM per instance and a browser binary in the image, which tripled our container size for output we could not tell apart in review.

Failed renders are retried three times with exponential backoff starting at 2 seconds, and a report that fails all three attempts raises an alert instead of being silently dropped: silent drops meant users learned about the failure from an empty inbox a day later.
Money amounts in reports are stored and rendered as integer minor units (cents), never as floats: a rounding mismatch between the report and the invoice cost us a week of reconciliation in March.

Report templates live in the service repository, not in the CMS. The CMS route was rejected because a template change could then reach production without review, and templates carry financial figures.

Every report includes the timezone it was generated in, next to the date range. Without it, a report covering 'March' meant different things to the Almaty and Lisbon offices and both thought the other was wrong.

A per-user custom report builder was proposed and rejected: it turns every report into an unbounded query against the warehouse, and the three requests we got were all covered by adding two fixed report types.
Generated report files are kept in S3 for 90 days and then deleted by a lifecycle rule; the underlying data stays in the warehouse, so any report can be regenerated.

Reports are generated in the requesting user's language, falling back to English when a template translation is missing rather than failing the render: a missing string is a cosmetic problem, a failed monthly report is an escalation.
Scheduled report jobs are limited to 5 concurrent renders per account.
The nightly aggregation job starts at 02:00 UTC.
Report exports are available in PDF and CSV only; XLSX was dropped because the library we used produced files Excel refused to open on Windows, and CSV covered every request we had.
Access to another user's report is granted through the account-admin role: admins can read every report inside their own account.
Report access is strictly per-user: nobody, including account admins, can read a report generated by another user. Financial reports fall under the data-minimisation rule from the security review.
